message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Confirmed **11 relevant vendor advisory bundles** newly published or made public during the last 24 hours. Highest priority is the Oracle MySQL CPU (CVSS up to 9.8), Google Chrome 156 (critical fixes), and Apache Tomcat's newly public Important issues.

**Scope:** Combined and deduplicated entries from `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt` only. `DLL_software_component.txt` was not read or combined.

**Scan window:** 2026-10-19 23:40 UTC through 2026-10-20 23:40 UTC (2026-10-20 05:10 IST through 2026-10-21 05:10 IST).

### Finding 1: Oracle MySQL October 2026 CPU

- **Product:** MySQL Server, Cluster, Client, Connectors, Router, and Enterprise Backup
- **Issue:** 98 new security patches; leading entries include CVE-2026-9547 and CVE-2025-15467
- **Severity:** Critical, CVSS up to 9.8
- **Description:** Oracle reports that 29 vulnerabilities may be remotely exploitable without authentication. The highest-rated issues affect MySQL Server/Cluster and Enterprise Backup through bundled curl or OpenSSL components.
- **Relevance:** MySQL and MySQL Workbench are in the monitored inventory.
- **Source:** [Oracle October 2026 Critical Patch Update](https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/cpuoct2026.html)

### Finding 2: Oracle Java SE October 2026 CPU

- **Product:** Oracle Java SE, JavaFX, and related GraalVM distributions
- **Issue:** 55 new security patches, including CVE-2026-43660 and CVE-2026-91484
- **Severity:** High, CVSS up to 7.5
- **Description:** Oracle states that 49 issues may be remotely exploitable without authentication. Affected versions include Java SE 8u503, 11.0.32.1, 17.0.20.1, 21.0.12.1, 25.0.4.1, and 27, depending on the CVE.
- **Relevance:** Oracle Java is explicitly monitored.
- **Source:** [Oracle October 2026 Critical Patch Update](https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/cpuoct2026.html)

### Finding 3: Oracle VM VirtualBox October 2026 CPU

- **Product:** Oracle VM VirtualBox
- **Issue:** Six vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-87322, CVE-2026-87301, and CVE-2026-101598
- **Severity:** High, CVSS up to 8.4
- **Description:** Oracle lists adjacent-network and local attack paths affecting VirtualBox Core. None are described as remotely exploitable without authentication.
- **Relevance:** VirtualBox 6.0.24 appears in the monitored inventory.
- **Source:** [Oracle October 2026 Critical Patch Update](https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/cpuoct2026.html)

### Finding 4: Google Chrome 156 security release

- **Product:** Google Chrome desktop and Android
- **Issue:** 353 security fixes; critical examples are CVE-2026-113341, CVE-2026-113279, and CVE-2026-113072
- **Severity:** Critical through Low
- **Description:** Google released Chrome 156.0.8078.47/.48 for desktop and 156.0.8078.47 for Android. The disclosed issues include memory-corruption, use-after-free, out-of-bounds-read, and input-validation flaws.
- **Relevance:** Google Chrome is explicitly monitored.
- **Source:** [Chrome Stable Channel Update for Desktop](https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/2026/10/stable-channel-update-for-desktop_02018666648.html)

### Finding 5: Apache Tomcat vulnerabilities made public

- **Product:** Apache Tomcat 9, 10.1, and 11
- **Issue:** Multiple CVEs, led by CVE-2026-103119, CVE-2026-101356, and CVE-2026-101296
- **Severity:** Important and Low, using Apache's ratings
- **Description:** Important issues include AJP response mix-up, HTTP/2 request/response mix-up, and a JNDIRealm authentication failure that could accept an incorrect password in affected configurations. Additional low-rated issues affect TLS cleanup, HTTP/2 trailers, JSTL redirects, Unix-domain-socket permissions, and FIPS fail-open behavior.
- **Relevance:** Apache Tomcat is explicitly monitored.
- **Source:** [Tomcat 9 advisories](https://tomcat.apache.org/security-9), [Tomcat 10 advisories](https://tomcat.apache.org/security-10), and [Tomcat 11 advisories](https://tomcat.apache.org/security-11)

### Finding 6: Mozilla Firefox 158.0.1 and ESR security updates

- **Product:** Firefox and Firefox ESR
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-113399, CVE-2026-113470, CVE-2026-113400, and CVE-2026-113401
- **Severity:** High to Low
- **Description:** Mozilla fixed SVG boundary handling, certificate block-list handling, uninitialized audio/video memory, and PDF Viewer denial-of-service issues. CVE-2026-113470 also applies to ESR 153.5.1 and 115.43.1.
- **Relevance:** Mozilla Firefox is explicitly monitored.
- **Source:** [MFSA 2026-111](https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-111/), [MFSA 2026-112](https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-112/), and [MFSA 2026-113](https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-113/)

### Finding 7: Ubuntu XZ Utils vulnerability

- **Product:** Ubuntu / XZ Utils
- **Issue:** Invalid memory write during decoder reinitialization
- **Severity:** Not clearly stated by Canonical
- **Description:** Specially crafted compressed files may trigger denial of service or, under some conditions, arbitrary code execution.
- **Relevance:** Ubuntu is explicitly monitored; the notice covers Ubuntu 14.04 through 26.10.
- **Source:** [Ubuntu USN-8945-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8945-1)

### Finding 8: Ubuntu .NET security update

- **Product:** Ubuntu-packaged .NET 8, 10, and 11
- **Issue:** 28 CVEs addressed in updated upstream releases
- **Severity:** Not clearly summarized by Canonical
- **Description:** Canonical published updated .NET runtimes and SDKs for Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, 26.04, and 26.10 to resolve multiple security issues.
- **Relevance:** Ubuntu and Microsoft .NET are both explicitly monitored.
- **Source:** [Ubuntu USN-8942-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8942-1)

### Finding 9: Ubuntu Protocol Buffers denial of service

- **Product:** Ubuntu / Protocol Buffers PHP library
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-6409
- **Severity:** Not clearly stated by Canonical
- **Description:** Improper handling of negative varint lengths and recursion limits can crash applications or exhaust resources when parsing crafted input.
- **Relevance:** This is an official Ubuntu package advisory, and Ubuntu is monitored.
- **Source:** [Ubuntu USN-8943-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8943-1)

### Finding 10: Ubuntu sudo-rs privilege escalation

- **Product:** Ubuntu 26.10 / sudo-rs
- **Issue:** Time-of-check/time-of-use flaw in sudoedit
- **Severity:** Not clearly stated by Canonical
- **Description:** A local user already permitted to edit specific files with sudoedit may place files in arbitrary directories and potentially elevate privileges. The affected fine-grained configuration is not the default.
- **Relevance:** Ubuntu is explicitly monitored.
- **Source:** [Ubuntu USN-8708-2](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8708-2)

### Finding 11: Ubuntu Squid vulnerabilities

- **Product:** Ubuntu / Squid
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-61642, CVE-2026-50012, CVE-2026-47729, CVE-2026-32748, CVE-2026-33526, and CVE-2026-33515
- **Severity:** Not clearly summarized by Canonical
- **Description:** The bundle addresses HTTP request smuggling and cache poisoning, denial of service, and information-disclosure weaknesses. Several issues affect only older Ubuntu releases.
- **Relevance:** These are official Ubuntu package fixes; Ubuntu is monitored.
- **Source:** [Ubuntu USN-8941-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8941-1)

### Possible matches needing review

None.

### MongoDB ecosystem verification

The mandatory dedicated sweep checked MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, `mongod`, `mongos`, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, `mongosh`, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, official drivers and connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, official integrations, maintained libraries, MongoDB-owned alerts, CVE/NVD records, GitHub Security Advisories, and CISA sources. No credible MongoDB-family vulnerability was newly reported or materially updated in the scan window. The newest entries on the [MongoDB Alerts page](https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/alerts) are dated October 13, 2026 and were excluded as stale.

### Review priority

Immediate review is recommended for exposed MySQL deployments and Chrome endpoints because the vendor bundles include Critical issues. Tomcat installations should also be checked promptly for affected 9.0, 10.1, or 11 versions and configurations. Oracle Java, VirtualBox, Firefox, and the Ubuntu package updates should follow in the normal priority queue based on deployed versions.
